title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
RT-ProtoNet: radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype networks for cross-region bathymetry in optically clear reef environments
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry faces two coupled obstacles: labels are scarce, and models transfer poorly across regions. We propose RT-ProtoNet, a radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype network, which takes patches from three penetrating Sentinel-2 bands and treats ICESat-2 depths, aggregated to the 10 m grid, as sparse supervision; cross-region episodic meta-training then yields a transferable metric representation. Rather than embedding the radiative transfer relation as an analytic formula, we use it as a comparability criterion between support and query pixels, entering the attention as a learnable additive distance penalty. The prediction sums a convex combination over support depths and a base regression head trained on source domains only and frozen at deployment, so no target-domain parameters are estimated. We evaluate on five optically clear shallow reef regions by leave-one-region-out cross-validation against airborne laser bathymetry, against nine baselines, where K is the total number of support pixels (3, 5, 10, 20, 50). For K ≤ 20, RT-ProtoNet attains the lowest cross-region macro-mean RMSE (2.79–2.48 m), with a run-to-run standard deviation 0.67 times the runner-up’s; at K = 50, pre-training with head fine-tuning overtakes it. Ablation shows the residual head’s gain scales with support depth coverage (correlation 0.991) and that the two physical priors are largely substitutable; twelve perturbations to the attenuation input change RMSE by only 0.66%. The method suits depths of roughly 2–20 m and budgets of K ≤ 20, and does not extrapolate to turbid or optically complex waters. Independent evaluation at two external optical-domain sites, a moderately turbid embayment (Tampa Bay) and a clear-to-moderately-turbid transition site (Boquerón Bay), further delineates the method’s applicability across contrasting optical conditions, showing reliable transfer within the clear-water regime but substantial degradation under stronger optical attenuation.

title: N-PCLN: A physics-informed deep learning framework for short-term chlorophyll-a prediction with sparse satellite observation
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Chlorophyll-a (Chla) is a key indicator of lake eutrophication. Its short-term prediction is essential for water quality monitoring and bloom early warning. However, traditional deep learning models often rely heavily on dense observations and provide limited process interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework, named N-PCLN, for short-term Chla prediction in Erhai Lake. The framework integrates Sentinel-3 OLCI imagery and meteorological datasets from 2016 to 2024. It uses Chla, land surface temperature, wind speed, and precipitation as inputs. Total phosphorus is incorporated through a nutrient–phytoplankton model to construct a physical loss. This design enables the model to jointly learn spatiotemporal patterns and nutrient–phytoplankton process constraints. The N-PCLN outperforms ConvLSTM, Transformer, MDN, CNN, and LSTM models, achieving an R 2 of 0.767, an MAE of 1.483 mg/m 3 , and an RMSE of 2.665 mg/m 3 . Sparse-data experiments show that N-PCLN maintains more stable performance than the selected baseline models under reduced data availability. The ablation experiments indicate that LST is the dominant meteorological factor driver of short-term Chla dynamics, while wind speed and precipitation mainly affect hydrodynamic redistribution and runoff-related nutrient transport. Physical-loss gradient analysis further reveals that the N-P constraint acts differently across seasons and Chla concentration. These results demonstrate that N-PCLN improves both prediction performance and process interpretability. It provides a useful framework for satellite-based lake water quality prediction.

title: Assessing the spatio-temporal cumulative drought effects on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Droughts are long-lasting events that can drive persistent functional changes in ecosystems, particularly in drought-prone areas like Mediterranean forests. We integrated a phenology-based anomaly method, combining kernel density estimation (KDE) with cumulative sums (CUSUMs) to assess long-term drought impacts on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile. Using MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), the Moisture Stress Index (MSI), and Evapotranspiration (ET) from 2000 to 2024, we quantified cumulative deviations in canopy productivity, moisture conditions, and energy exchange. Our framework revealed persistent negative functional trajectories preceding the well-documented 2010–present megadrought. Spatially explicit metrics identified coherent degradation hotspots in northern sclerophyllous and southern deciduous forests, where canopy greenness, moisture, and evapotranspiration declined synchronously. Seasonal models indicated a post-2010 strengthening of soil–water controls over forest functioning, with soil moisture and water storage variables becoming influential predictors. The convergence of cumulative negative EVI, MSI, and ET signals highlights widespread and sustained functional weakening under prolonged drought conditions. Our results demonstrate that integrating KDE-derived anomalies with cumulative deviation tracking provides a sensitive and transferable framework to detect early and persistent vegetation stress in water-limited ecosystems.

title: Deep learning detection of submesoscale eddies from MODIS SST in the South China Sea
abstract: This dataset provides daily records of submesoscale eddies in the South China Sea from 2015 to 2024, identified from MODIS Aqua and Terra sea surface temperature (SST) imagery. Distributed as daily TXT files, each record includes eddy polarity, center coordinates (longitude and latitude), and eddy diameter.

title: Unsupervised Clustering of Public Transport Vehicles Using Deep Morphological Features and Color Histograms
abstract: Surveillance cameras along urban roads produce large volumes of unlabeled video that could support the monitoring of public transport, but grouping the observed vehicles into meaningful categories without manual annotation remains challenging, since buses from different routes often share the same body structure and differ mainly in their color schemes. This study presents an unsupervised clustering methodology for public transport vehicles that combines morphological features extracted with a frozen DINOv2 Vision Transformer and handcrafted HSV color histograms through weighted early fusion, followed by UMAP projection and K-Means clustering. The method was evaluated on 7,972 bus images extracted from about 1,460 hours of video of an arterial road in Mexico City, with the goal of isolating the buses of the city's public bus network (RTP) without supervision. With a fusion of 65\% morphological and 35\% color features, the pipeline produced 14 clusters that separate distinct routes and vehicle types, and it increased the precision of the target cluster with respect to morphological features alone. These results show that color complements self-supervised features for route-level clustering, provided that it does not dominate the representation.
